findings.reproduction: A later inbound window was added to present on-hand before the depletion calculation, allowing a pre-arrival stock gap to appear safe.
findings.rootCause: Current supply and future dated supply were represented as one fungible scalar instead of a governed time-phased schedule.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned every future-supply aggregation; inbound now changes projected supply only at its conservative eligible instant and stale/cancelled/conflicted/overdue states never supply safety.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRiskFlowIT persists the time-phased calculation and exact evidence links in PostgreSQL.

findings.reproduction: A fresh nonpositive Settled result could collapse into unavailable and fall through to a positive Operational result.
findings.rootCause: Nullable profit authority conflated unavailable, authoritative-positive and authoritative-nonpositive states.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned Optional/nullable business-authority collapse paths and retained an explicit unavailable state distinct from an authoritative numeric result.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRiskFlowIT exercises Settled/Operational projection selection through real persisted metrics.

findings.reproduction: Facts sharing a timestamp at a page boundary could be skipped by the timestamp-only cursor; crash replay could not prove total order.
findings.rootCause: The feed cursor did not persist the complete durable keyset ordering tuple.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned timestamp-only keyset cursors; accepted facts now order by `(ingestion_time, provenance_id, item_key)` with durable first-start and monotonic replay semantics.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRecalculationLoopIT proves same-timestamp paging, first-start backfill and idempotent crash replay against PostgreSQL.

findings.reproduction: The reconciliation job stopped at a hard row cap, delayed completion and did not prove a full portfolio could finish hourly.
findings.rootCause: A capped batch was treated as a complete sweep and progress/failure were not represented as durable run state.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned every hard row cap described as full; reconciliation now keyset-pages the declared portfolio, persists progress, isolates per-Variant failure and records incomplete/recovered runs.
findings.runtimeEvidence: RepresentativePerformanceIT executes a real 5,000-Variant full sweep, records wall time/hourly margin and repairs 50 deliberately dropped triggers.

findings.reproduction: Company demand divided combined sales by the maximum single-channel exposure, understating demand when channel availability intervals were disjoint.
findings.rootCause: Cross-channel exposure was reduced to one scalar maximum rather than an attributable union of intervals.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned demand/exposure aggregation and replaced cross-channel maximum exposure with interval-union semantics that preserve overlap, disjoint periods, censoring and gaps.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRiskFlowIT persists selected demand windows and their attributable exposure evidence.

findings.reproduction: A same-tenant caller with one Store/Product grant could reach queue/card/child resources outside that owned scope.
findings.rootCause: Authorization stopped at Organization ownership and direct-ID reads did not rebind loaded resources to Store/Product/Data/Action scope.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned all direct-ID reads/mutations and pagination/filter paths for loaded-resource scope authorization, including same-tenant sibling Product and Store bypass attempts.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityConsoleAuthorizationIT proves absence/refusal semantics using real grants and PostgreSQL resources.

findings.reproduction: A public human endpoint could mark an unresolved Case `VERIFIED_SUCCESS` without fresh calculated outcome authority.
findings.rootCause: Human action evidence and canonical outcome verification shared one externally writable transition surface.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned every human endpoint and state transition capable of canonical success; people may record structured action evidence, while only fresh cause-specific calculations may verify.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Browser `TC-BROWSER-014` exercises action, automatic verification and same-Case reopen against the real backend.

findings.reproduction: Exception decision identifiers could be combined across Organizations/resources because the service authorized supplied IDs rather than the loaded owned graph.
findings.rootCause: Exception, Case, risk child and Organization identities were not relationally bound and authorization did not operate on the loaded aggregate.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned exception/request/decision mutations for supplied-ID trust; service and database constraints now bind the complete owned resource graph and requester/approver separation.
findings.runtimeEvidence: PostgreSQL foreign keys/checks reject cross-tenant and unrelated-resource combinations independently of the service.

findings.reproduction: A missing company demand policy aborted the complete calculation and suppressed an independently exact Channel stockout.
findings.rootCause: Channel and company calculations shared an all-or-nothing policy-resolution gate.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned queries/calculations that dropped independent Channel identity when company authority failed; channel results now compute independently and company policy defects route separately.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRiskFlowIT persists the exact Channel child while separately persisting a company blocker child.

findings.reproduction: Demand/availability evidence lost exact fulfillment-mode identity and began the observation window without the last authoritative pre-window exposure state.
findings.rootCause: Fact queries aggregated above Store/mode/as-of identity and initialized exposure from only in-window facts.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned availability/demand queries for dropped Store/mode/as-of/freshness; exact mode is preserved or fails closed and windows seed from the latest authoritative pre-window state.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Real PostgreSQL facts prove pre-window seeding and mode-specific evidence provenance.

findings.reproduction: Carry-forward could activate when only one demand window was censored, allowing a mixed verdict to reuse historical demand.
findings.rootCause: The predicate used any-window censoring rather than the accepted all-windows-censored condition.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned carry-forward predicates and encoded the exact truth table: every governed window must be censored and the prior eligible period must remain fresh and bounded.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRiskFlowIT exposes carry-forward source period, expiry and confidence downgrade in stored evidence.

findings.reproduction: Company available supply omitted live QC lock, damage/write-off and sellability authority and could count non-sellable units.
findings.rootCause: Warehouse stock facts did not carry the material stock-state inputs used by the accepted company-supply formula.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned stale stock/ownership values used as current supply; reservation, QC lock, damaged/written-off and sellability facts are current, attributable and fail closed when material state is absent.
findings.runtimeEvidence: OperatingFlowIT and AvailabilityRiskFlowIT ingest and calculate from the expanded stock-state facts through PostgreSQL.

findings.reproduction: Retained/Return/Refusal/QC evidence and returned-stock ledger re-entry semantics were absent, so the quality Guardrail could not run end to end.
findings.rootCause: The Slice had a quality label but no durable report-coverage authority, policy freshness, return/QC lane or governed inventory transition chain.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned fixture-only quality authority; append-only snapshots now distinguish no evidence, zero-return evidence, stale, incomplete, conflicted and observed-return coverage, while returned supply requires the exact QC/re-entry chain.
findings.runtimeEvidence: OperatingFlowIT proves transport-to-QC-to-ledger-reentry linkage; AvailabilityRiskSchemaIT proves append-only quality evidence and freshness policy schema.

findings.reproduction: Inbound attestation and required availability policies existed mostly as fixture/read paths without governed application/API mutation lifecycles.
findings.rootCause: Policy and inbound authority were modeled as calculation inputs but not as attributable, effective-dated, audited user capabilities.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned fixture-only authorities falsely marked complete; inbound and policy create/amend/reverify/cancel/publish flows enforce role/resource scope, effective time, audit, conflict and targeted recalculation.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Browser and PostgreSQL integration paths exercise the governed authority surfaces with synthetic isolated identities.

findings.reproduction: Priority weights were hard-coded and excluded from the stored projection/card policy identity.
findings.rootCause: Ranking configuration lived in code instead of an attributable effective-dated policy authority.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned policy constants excluded from evidence identity; every ranking factor resolves through a versioned policy whose exact digest participates in projection/card identity.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityRiskFlowIT stores and reads back the exact priority policy digest with the triggering child.

findings.reproduction: An accepted exception remained active after risk/materiality/cause/scope/authority/recurrence/evidence/policy drift.
findings.rootCause: Validity was checked only when the exception was approved or expired, not continuously against current typed authority and risk snapshots.
findings.sameClassScan: Scanned every exception invalidation condition; accepted snapshots, direct/delegated authority and current policy/evidence are re-evaluated on change and sweep, with one-time delegation revocation and same-Case reopen/escalation.
findings.runtimeEvidence: AvailabilityConsoleAuthorizationIT executes grant, delegated approval, revoke, automatic `AUTHORITY_LOST` invalidation and same-Case escalation against PostgreSQL.
